paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. Ben-hadad shows up with thirty-two kings, and Ahab says yes to the silver, gold, wives and children, then says no when Ben-hadad wants to search the houses and seize what is precious. Then the LORD sends a prophet with a word: "Behold, I will deliver it into your hand this very day, and you will know that I am the LORD." (1 Kings 20:13) The size of the army outside the wall was never the biggest thing in this story.

Now look at HOW the LORD does it. He says it will happen "By the young officers of the district governors." (1 Kings 20:14) Two hundred thirty-two young officers against a pile of kings, and I think that's the point. When the win comes from somewhere nobody expected, nobody gets to say it came from them, and that's how Ahab would know it was the LORD.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Some days the other side has more of everything: more bills, more noise, more people who seem to be winning. Don't measure the day by the size of what's standing at your gate. Measure it by who sent the word. And hang on to your apron, because this story is not finished.
